literal: Cui Jishu; Zu Ting
idiomatic: Cui Jishu; Zu Ting

literal: Cui Jishu, styled Shuzheng, was a man of Anping in Boling.
idiomatic: Cui Jishu, styled Shuzheng, came from Anping in Boling commandery.

literal: His father Yuzhi was Chamberlain for Dependent States under Wei.
idiomatic: His father Yuzhi had been Wei chamberlain for dependent states.

literal: Jishu was orphaned young; by nature bright and keen, he ranged through the classics and histories, excelled at correspondence, and had the talent and equipment of his age.
idiomatic: Orphaned young, Jishu was bright and quick, read widely in classics and histories, wrote excellent dispatches, and had real gifts for his time.

literal: At seventeen he was chief clerk of the province; the Grand General, Duke of Zhao commandery Chen, valued him highly and spoke of him to Gao Huan.
idiomatic: At seventeen he served as provincial chief clerk. Grand General the Duke of Zhao commandery, Chen, favored him and recommended him to Gao Huan.

literal: Gao Huan personally screened chancellery and department men and appointed Jishu lang in the Mobile Grand Secretariat Bureau of Offices.
idiomatic: Gao Huan personally screened chancellery and department officers and made Jishu lang in the mobile grand secretariat bureau of offices.

literal: When Gao Cheng took up regency he was transferred to staff officer in the grand general central troops bureau and was greatly favored.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng assumed regency, Jishu was moved to staff officer in the grand general central troops bureau and won close favor.

literal: Because the Wei emperor needed trusted men at his side, Jishu was promoted secretariat gentleman.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor needed trusted men at his side, so Jishu was promoted secretariat gentleman.

literal: Gao Cheng was supervisor of the secretariat; the business of the Secretariat Gate was folded into the secretariat, and because Jishu was skilled at music the inner performers also reported through him—the inner performers belonged to the secretariat.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng supervised the secretariat; secretariat-gate business was folded into it. Because Jishu knew music, inner palace performers also came under him—inner performers now belonged to the secretariat.

literal: This began with Jishu.
idiomatic: That practice began with Jishu.

literal: Whenever Gao Cheng presented memorials to the Wei emperor with remonstrances, if the wording grew tangled Jishu would polish and render it clear so only the admonition stood forth.
idiomatic: Whenever Gao Cheng sent the Wei emperor memorials with remonstrance, Jishu would trim tangled wording so the counsel itself could pass.

literal: Emperor Jing, when answering the hegemonic court, always discussed it with Jishu, saying, "Secretariat Gentleman Cui is our wet nurse.
idiomatic: When Emperor Jing drafted replies to the hegemonic court, he always discussed them with Jishu and said, "Secretariat Gentleman Cui is our wet nurse.

literal: " He was transferred to gentleman of the yellow gate and concurrently oversaw the directorate of imperial wardrobe.
idiomatic: " He was then made gentleman of the yellow gate and also oversaw the directorate of imperial wardrobe.

literal: Though his footprints lay in the Wei court, his heart belonged to the hegemonic government; on weighty plans he was always allowed to hear in advance.
idiomatic: Though he still walked the Wei court, his heart was with the hegemonic government, and he was let in early on major plans.

literal: Guests then gathered in numbers; he received them with open courtesy and won a great name, until his power outshone Cui Xian.
idiomatic: Guests gathered in force; he met them with open courtesy, won wide renown, and his power eclipsed Cui Xian.

literal: Once Xian at the hall dismissed others and bowed to him, saying, "If Xian should obtain vice director of the masters of writing, it is all Uncle's grace.
idiomatic: Once at court Xian dismissed everyone else and bowed to him, saying, "If Xian wins vice director of the masters of writing, it will be entirely my uncle's favor.

literal: " Such was his weight in power.
idiomatic: " His weight in power was such.

literal: At that time many meritorious nobles acted lawlessly; Gao Cheng would not spare them, and outsiders blamed Jishu and Cui Xian and others for it and bitterly resented them.
idiomatic: Many meritorious nobles then broke the law, and Gao Cheng would not spare them. Outsiders blamed Jishu, Cui Xian, and the rest, and hated them bitterly.

literal: When Gao Cheng met disaster, Gao Yang was about to go to Jinyang; Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiuzhi urged Jishu to go along, saying, "One day without attending court, and in between a blade may be hidden.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was killed, Gao Yang was bound for Jinyang. Gentleman of the yellow gate Yang Xiuzhi urged Jishu to go with him, saying, "Miss one day at court and a blade may hide in the interval.

literal: " Jishu loved music and women; his heart was set on leisure, so he did not ask to go and meant to indulge his pleasures.
idiomatic: " Jishu loved music and women and wanted leisure, so he did not ask to go and meant to enjoy himself.

literal: Sima Ziru, nursing an old grudge, together with Director of Palace Provisions Chen Shanti and others jointly listed his offenses, and thereby Jishu and Xian were each flogged two hundred strokes and sent to the northern marches.
idiomatic: Sima Ziru, holding an old grudge, joined Director of Palace Provisions Chen Shanti and others in listing his offenses. Jishu and Xian were each flogged two hundred strokes and exiled north.

literal: Early in Tianbao Gao Yang knew they were guiltless and recalled Jishu as director of imperial works, then again promoted him to regular attendant.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao, Gao Yang knew they were innocent and recalled Jishu as director of imperial works, then promoted him again to regular attendant.

literal: Soon he was concurrently made left vice director of the masters of writing and ceremonial peer of the three ranks, and was deeply favored.
idiomatic: Soon he was also left vice director of the masters of writing and ceremonial peer of the three ranks, and was deeply favored.

literal: Early in Qianming Yang Yin, on Gao Yang dying instruction, stopped his vice directorship.
idiomatic: Early in Qianming, Yang Yin, acting on Gao Yang's final instruction, removed him from vice director.

literal: On his mother mourning he left office; recalled from mourning he was made director of splendid happiness and concurrently chief of the central troops bureau in the masters of writing.
idiomatic: He left office for his mother mourning, then was recalled and made director of splendid happiness while also chief of the central troops bureau in the masters of writing.

literal: Sent out as governor of Qi province; because he sent men across the Huai for mutual trade and had bribery matters as well, he was impeached by the censorate, but pardoned and not pursued.
idiomatic: Sent out as governor of Qi, he was impeached for sending men across the Huai to trade and for bribery as well, but was pardoned and not pursued.

literal: When Gao Zhan held a princely fief he once fell ill; Gao Yang ordered Jishu to treat him and he spared no effort.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhan held a princely fief he once fell ill; Gao Yang ordered Jishu to treat him, and Jishu spared no effort.

literal: Early in Daning he was recalled, brought in and comforted, and repeatedly promoted to director of revenue in the masters of writing and grand ceremonial peer opening a government office.
idiomatic: Early in Daning he was recalled, comforted at court, and promoted in turn to director of revenue in the masters of writing and grand ceremonial peer with an opened government office.

literal: When the Zhaoyang Palace was being built he was ordered to oversee construction.
idiomatic: When the Zhaoyang Palace was raised, he was ordered to oversee construction.

literal: Because in a case-review form Hu Changren privately denounced his faults, he was sent out as governor of Western Yanzhou.
idiomatic: Hu Changren privately denounced his faults in a case-review form, and he was sent out as governor of Western Yanzhou.

literal: Serving as advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and removed from office; again for visiting the mansion of Prince of Guangning he was sentenced to several dozen strokes of the horsewhip.
idiomatic: As advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and dismissed; for visiting Prince of Guangning mansion he was also sentenced to several dozen horsewhip strokes.

literal: When Gao Zhan died he was not allowed to take part in the mourning rites.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhan died he was not allowed to join the mourning rites.

literal: After a long interval he was made governor of Jiao province, then transferred to regular attendant and grand ceremonial peer, with salary from the two commanderies of Xinan and Heyin.
idiomatic: Long afterward he was made governor of Jiao, then regular attendant and grand ceremonial peer, drawing salary from Xin'an and Heyin commanderies.

literal: Advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
idiomatic: He was advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.

literal: Made special advancement and supervisor of the national history.
idiomatic: He was made special advancement and supervisor of the national history.

literal: Jishu had always loved books; in his later years he grew still more diligent, and he also recommended men and encouraged letters—opinion converged, and near and far praised him.
idiomatic: Jishu had always loved books and grew keener in old age. He also recommended men and encouraged letters; opinion converged, and praise spread near and far.

literal: Zu Ting received a commission and memorialized that Jishu should oversee inner construction altogether.
idiomatic: Zu Ting received a commission and memorialized that Jishu should oversee all inner construction.

literal: When Ting was sent out, Han Changluan thought him an associate of Ting and wished to send Jishu out as well.
idiomatic: When Ting was sent out, Han Changluan treated him as Ting's man and wanted to send Jishu out too.

literal: As the imperial carriage was about to visit Jinyang, Jishu and Zhang Diao discussed: Shouchun was besieged, the great army went out to resist, and couriers went back and forth requiring orders from headquarters;
idiomatic: As the emperor was about to go to Jinyang, Jishu and Zhang Diao argued that with Shouchun besieged and the main army out to resist, couriers would need headquarters orders;

literal: moreover petty men on the road might spread alarm, saying the great carriage was heading for Bing, fleeing the southern foe;
idiomatic: and petty men on the road might panic, saying the court was fleeing to Bing to avoid the southern enemy;

literal: if they did not memorialize in remonstrance, the people's hearts would certainly be shaken.
idiomatic: if no remonstrance were submitted, the people's hearts would surely be shaken.

literal: They then joined with the civil officials in the retinue in a joint remonstrance by signature.
idiomatic: They therefore joined the civil officials in the retinue in a joint signed remonstrance.

literal: At the time the great ministers Zhao Yanshen, Tang Yong, and Duan Xiaoyan had at first agreed in heart, but at the last moment grew doubtful—Jishu disputed with them without decision.
idiomatic: Great ministers Zhao Yanshen, Tang Yong, and Duan Xiaoyan had first agreed, then wavered at the last moment; Jishu argued with them without resolution.

literal: Changluan then memorialized, saying, "Han civil officials have jointly signed, voicing remonstrance against going to Bing when in fact they may well not be loyal—they should be put to death."
idiomatic: Changluan then memorialized: "Han civil officials signed together, claiming to stop the move to Bing, but may in fact be disloyal—they should be executed."

literal: The emperor at once summoned the officials who had signed the memorial to gather in the Hange Hall; taking Jishu, Zhang Diao, Liu Ti, Feng Xiaoyan, Pei Ze, Guo Zun, and others as ringleaders, he beheaded them all in the hall courtyard, and Changluan had their corpses cast into the Zhang River.
idiomatic: The emperor at once summoned every official who had signed to the Hange Hall. Jishu, Zhang Diao, Liu Ti, Feng Xiaoyan, Pei Ze, Guo Zun, and others were taken as ringleaders and beheaded in the courtyard; Changluan had their bodies thrown into the Zhang River.

literal: The others who had signed beyond that were to be flogged as well; Zhao Yanshen clasped remonstrance and they were spared.
idiomatic: The rest who had signed were to be flogged too, but Zhao Yanshen seized the emperor sleeve in remonstrance and they were spared.

literal: The households of Jishu and the rest, men and women, were sent to the northern marches; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were assigned to tribal wardens, young sons cast into the silkworm chamber, and property confiscated.
idiomatic: The households of Jishu and the others, men and women, were sent north; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were assigned to tribal wardens, young sons to the silkworm chamber, and property was confiscated.

literal: Jishu greatly loved medicine; in the Tianbao era, idle at his place of exile, he studied with sharpened purpose and became a master hand, saving many lives.
idiomatic: Jishu loved medicine deeply. In Tianbao, idle in exile, he studied harder still and became a master who saved many lives.

literal: Though his status and hopes grew higher, he never slackened; even for the poor and lowly in service he treated them.
idiomatic: Though rank and reputation rose, he never slackened; he treated even poor servants.

literal: His secondary son Changjun was outer-lang in the right section of military affairs in the masters of writing.
idiomatic: His secondary son Changjun was outer-lang in the right military affairs section of the masters of writing.

literal: Next Jingxuan was assistant in the compositions office.
idiomatic: Next came Jingxuan, assistant in the compositions office.

literal: Both were exiled to the far frontier.
idiomatic: Both were exiled to the far frontier.

literal: Before long the wives of the six men of Jishu and the rest, being old, were released.
idiomatic: Before long the wives of the six, being old, were released.

literal: Later Prince of Nanan Sihao again charged the court with crimes, taking the harm done to Jishu and the others as his pretext, and summoned the brothers and nephews of the six men sons to follow the army toward Jinyang.
idiomatic: Later Prince of Nanan Sihao again denounced the court crimes, citing the killing of Jishu and the others, and summoned the six men brothers and nephews to follow his army toward Jinyang.

literal: When the affair failed, Changjun and the rest were all killed with him; the six men wives were again taken into service in the palace.
idiomatic: When the affair failed, Changjun and the rest were executed with him, and the six wives were taken back into palace service.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi, an edict specially granted honors posthumously to Hulü Guang together with the six including Jishu; Jishu was posthumously granted grand ceremonial peer, general-in-chief opening a government office, and governor of Ding province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi, an edict granted posthumous honors to Hulü Guang and the six including Jishu; Jishu was made posthumous grand ceremonial peer, general-in-chief opening a government office, and governor of Ding.

literal: Zu Ting, styled Xiaozheng, was a man of Di Dao in Fanyang.
idiomatic: Zu Ting, styled Xiaozheng, came from Di Dao in Fanyang.

literal: His father Ying was defender-general of Wei.
idiomatic: His father Ying was Wei defender-general.

literal: Ting was alert in spirit and quick in wit, his diction forceful and fluent; from youth he won a fine reputation and was praised by the world.
idiomatic: Ting was quick-witted and alert, his phrasing forceful and fluent; from youth he won fame and the age praised him.

literal: He first took office as secretariat lang; in the policy-response examination he ranked high and became lang in the ritual protocols section of the masters of writing, in charge of ceremonial regulations.
idiomatic: He began as secretariat lang, ranked high in the policy examination, and became lang in the ritual protocols section of the masters of writing, in charge of ceremonial regulations.

literal: Once he composed for Wanqi Shouluo, governor of Ji province, the "Eulogy of Pure Virtue"; the text was classical and beautiful, and thereby Gao Huan heard of him.
idiomatic: Once he wrote the "Eulogy of Pure Virtue" for Ji governor Wanqi Shouluo; the text was elegant, and Gao Huan heard of him.

literal: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing province and appointed Ting army-camp staff officer opening a government office.
idiomatic: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing and appointed Ting army-camp staff officer with an opened government office.

literal: Gao Huan dictated thirty-six items to Ting; when he came out Ting wrote them up in a memorial and not one was lost—greatly admired by colleagues.
idiomatic: Gao Huan dictated thirty-six items to Ting; Ting wrote them into a memorial without losing one, and colleagues admired him greatly.

literal: Then Gao Huan was sending Princess Lanling of Wei beyond the frontier to marry the Rouran; Wei Shou composed two pieces, "Crossing the Frontier" and "The Princess Far Marriage"; Ting harmonized with both, and they were widely chanted in the age.
idiomatic: Then Gao Huan was sending Princess Lanling of Wei beyond the frontier to marry the Rouran. Wei Shou wrote "Crossing the Frontier" and "The Princess Far Marriage"; Ting harmonized with both, and the age chanted them widely.

literal: Ting was by nature careless and coarse, unable to keep integrity and caution in office.
idiomatic: Ting was careless by nature and could not keep office with integrity and caution.

literal: Though the army-camp post was called a provincial bureau, he received the levies from east of the mountains and thereby took bribes in great quantity, growing rich in assets.
idiomatic: Though the army-camp post was called a provincial bureau, he took levies from east of the mountains, accepted bribes in quantity, and grew very rich.

literal: He himself could play the pipa and compose new tunes; he summoned city youths to sing and dance for pleasure and frequented every singing-house.
idiomatic: He could play pipa and compose new tunes, gathered city youths to sing and dance for pleasure, and haunted singing-houses.

literal: With Chen Yuankang, Mu Zirong, Ren Zhou, Yuan Shiliang, and others he indulged in music and women.
idiomatic: With Chen Yuankang, Mu Zirong, Ren Zhou, Yuan Shiliang, and others he pursued music and women.

literal: When the men once lodged with Ting, he brought out from east of the mountains large-pattern damask and linked-pearl peacock gauze and the like, more than a hundred bolts, and had the women cast dice for stakes as a pastime.
idiomatic: When they once lodged with him, he brought out east-of-the-mountains damask and linked-pearl peacock gauze, more than a hundred bolts, and had the women gamble at dice for sport.

literal: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of the former minister over the masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, born of the former Wei emperor Jing aunt, the Princess of Boling the Great.
idiomatic: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of former Minister over the Masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, child of Emperor Jing aunt, the great Princess of Boling.

literal: Ting suddenly brought Jingxian wife to the feast and shared her in turn with the company—this too came from greed for goods.
idiomatic: Ting suddenly brought Jingxian wife to the feast and passed her among the company in turn—again for gain.

literal: So wild and dissolute was he.
idiomatic: His license was such.

literal: He often said, "A man in one lifetime must not fail his person."
idiomatic: He often said, "A man lives once and must not betray his body."

literal: After Gao Yang left his provincial post Ting should by rule follow the headquarters; scheming for the grain-store post, he made request through Chen Yuankang, and Yuankang spoke for him, so he returned to the army-camp post.
idiomatic: After Gao Yang left the province Ting should have followed headquarters, but schemed for the grain-store post through Chen Yuankang, who spoke for him, and he returned to army-camp duty.

literal: Ting also threw himself on Chief Registry Clerk Lu Zixian, who held acting military staff duties, and together they drew up plans; at the time of requesting grain he had Zixian proclaim the order, and ten cartloads of granary grain were issued—caught by a colleague and sent for trial.
idiomatic: Ting also attached himself to chief registry clerk Lu Zixian, acting military staff officer, and they plotted together; when grain was requested Zixian proclaimed the order, ten cartloads were issued, and colleagues seized them for trial.

literal: Gao Huan questioned him in person; Ting said himself he had not received appointment and blamed Zixian, and Gao Huan believed him and released him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan questioned him in person. Ting said he had no commission and blamed Zixian; Gao Huan believed him and released him.

literal: Coming out he said, "This chancellor heaven-bestowed discernment—but in truth Xiaozheng did it."
idiomatic: Coming out he said, "The chancellor heaven-sent clarity sees through—but in truth Xiaozheng did it."

literal: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at the home of Governor of Jiao province Sima Shiyun and hid two bronze mirrors.
idiomatic: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at Jiao governor Sima Shiyun home and hid two bronze mirrors.

literal: The cook asked to search the guests; they were indeed found in Ting bosom, and witnesses thought it a deep shame.
idiomatic: The cook asked to search the guests; they were found in Ting bosom, and onlookers thought it deep shame.

literal: The old horse he rode he always called a piebald colt.
idiomatic: The old horse he rode he always called a piebald colt.

literal: He also committed adultery with the widow surnamed Wang, each time exchanging word before others.
idiomatic: He also lay with the widow Wang, exchanging messages openly before others.

literal: Pei Rangzhi was early intimate with Ting and before the crowd mocked him, saying, "How can you be so strange—an old horse of ten years still called a piebald colt;
idiomatic: Pei Rangzhi, long intimate with him, mocked him before the crowd: "How can you be so strange—a ten-year horse still called a piebald colt;

literal: a wife at sixty still called Mistress."
idiomatic: a sixty-year wife still called Mistress."

literal: At the time it spread with a roar.
idiomatic: The crowd roared and the story spread.

literal: Later he was merit officer in Gao Huan inner and outer government office; at a feast of subordinates Gao Huan lost a gold bowl, and Dou Tai ordered all who drank to remove their caps—in Ting topknot it was found; Gao Huan could not punish him.
idiomatic: Later he was merit officer in Gao Huan inner and outer government office. At a feast Gao Huan lost a gold bowl; Dou Tai made every drinker remove his cap—it was found in Ting's hair; Gao Huan could not punish him.

literal: Later he was secretariat assistant and led gentlemen-in-attendance, serving Gao Cheng.
idiomatic: Later he was secretariat assistant, leading gentlemen-in-attendance, serving Gao Cheng.

literal: A provincial visitor came asking to sell the Forest Compendium.
idiomatic: A provincial visitor came offering to sell the Forest Compendium.

literal: Gao Cheng gathered many copyists and in one day and one night finished the copy, then returned the original, saying, "Not needed."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng gathered copyists and finished a copy in one day and one night, then returned the original, saying, "Not needed."

literal: Ting pledged several volumes of the Compendium for dice stakes; Gao Cheng had him flogged forty.
idiomatic: Ting pledged several volumes of the Compendium for dice gambling; Gao Cheng had him flogged forty strokes.

literal: Again with clerk Li Shuang, granary overseer Cheng Zu, and others he drafted a Jinzhou memorial requesting three thousand shi of grain; standing in for merit officer Zhao Yanshen he proclaimed Gao Huan order and gave it to garrison-bureau merit officer and passing registry clerk Gao Jinglue, who doubted the quota was not real and secretly asked Yanshen; Yanshen answered there was no such matter at all—thereupon investigation was pushed, and Ting confessed at once.
idiomatic: Again with clerk Li Shuang, granary overseer Cheng Zu, and others he drafted a Jinzhou memorial for three thousand shi of grain; standing in for merit officer Zhao Yanshen he proclaimed Gao Huan order to garrison merit officer and passing registry clerk Gao Jinglue. Jinglue doubted the amount, secretly asked Yanshen, and Yanshen said there was no such order. Investigation followed, and Ting confessed at once.

literal: Gao Huan was greatly angered; sentenced him to two hundred strokes, assigned to the armor ward, and iron added; the grain was levied at double.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was furious: two hundred strokes, assignment to the armor ward, irons added, and the grain levied at double.

literal: Before the levy was exacted, the new Dingguo Temple in Bingzhou was completed; Gao Huan said to Chen Yuankang and Wen Zisheng, "When we composed the Mangshan Temple stele text it was called peerless—now for the Dingguo Temple stele whose words should compose it?
idiomatic: Before the levy was collected, the new Dingguo Temple in Bingzhou was finished. Gao Huan said to Chen Yuankang and Wen Zisheng, "The Mangshan Temple stele was called peerless—who should write the Dingguo Temple stele now?

literal: Yuankang thereupon recommended Ting learning and that he also understood Xianbei speech.
idiomatic: Yuankang recommended Ting learning and said he also understood Xianbei.

literal: Brush and paper were given and in the prison ward the draft was produced.
idiomatic: Brush and paper were sent, and he drafted it in confinement.

literal: Within two days it was finished; the text was very beautiful.
idiomatic: He finished in two days; the text was very fine.

literal: Gao Huan, because he was skilled and swift, especially pardoned and did not pursue, yet still removed him from office to serve scattered in the chancellor office.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, impressed by his skill and speed, especially pardoned him, though he still removed him from office to serve scattered in the chancellor office.

literal: When Gao Cheng took up the succession he made him merit officer in the army-camp.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took up the succession he made him army-camp merit officer.

literal: When Gao Cheng met disaster Yuankang wounds were grave; he had Ting compose a letter entrusting family burdens, and also said, "At the border Zu Xi has a little property—take it soon."
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was killed Yuankang wounds were grave; he had Ting write a letter entrusting family matters, and also said, "Zu Xi at the border has a little property—take it soon."

literal: Ting did not deliver this letter but summoned Zu Xi in private to ask; he got twenty-five ingots of gold and gave Xi only two—the rest all entered his own purse.
idiomatic: Ting did not deliver the letter but summoned Zu Xi privately; he got twenty-five ingots of gold, gave Xi only two, and kept the rest.

literal: He also stole several thousand scrolls of books from Yuankang's house.
idiomatic: He also stole several thousand scrolls from Yuankang's house.
